answer: One mechanism is a copper-backed identity bond: each agent locks a small, non-transferable deposit tied to a unique hardware secure element whose clock drift is fingerprinted by its quartz oscillator. Vouching creates a ripple of trust that counts only when bonds were registered through distinct devices and paid independently. Sybil clusters grow expensive and visible, since fake identities cannot reuse the same quartz signature or fabricate separate copper deposits without exposing correlated funding.
